claims.text: The Trinamool Congress faction led by former West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee filed a petition in the Supreme Court on September 18, 2026, challenging the Election Commission of India's decision to freeze the party's name and symbol.

On September 17, 2026, the Election Commission of India issued an interim order barring the use of the All India Trinamool Congress name and symbol in the upcoming West Bengal Assembly byelections in Nandigram and Rejinagar.

The Election Commission of India allotted the name 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress' and the 'football player' symbol to Mamata Banerjee's faction, while allotting 'Democratic Trinamool Congress' and the 'envelope' symbol to Ritabrata Banerjee's faction.
Mamata Banerjee's faction filed a petition in the Supreme Court highlighting delays in disqualification proceedings pending before the West Bengal Assembly Speaker against 10 rebel legislators.
Mamata Banerjee founded the All India Trinamool Congress in 1998 after splitting from the Indian National Congress and hand-drew its original 'Jora Ghas Phool' symbol.
Mamata Banerjee described the loss of her party's original name and symbol as a 'black day' in India's democratic history.
Both Trinamool Congress factions were recognized as political parties in West Bengal, Meghalaya, and Tripura.
Mamata Banerjee announced that her faction would not contest the Nandigram Assembly by-election and would instead support Congress candidate Milan Pradhan.
Sanchita Pradhan Dey, the candidate initially chosen by Mamata Banerjee's faction for the Nandigram bypoll, withdrew her nomination.
Congress candidate for the Nandigram Assembly by-election Milan Pradhan was arrested on September 18, 2026, in connection with a 2007 murder case.
Nearly 60 out of 80 Trinamool Congress MLAs in the West Bengal Assembly rebelled against party leadership following the May Assembly elections.
In June 2026, 20 out of 28 Trinamool Congress Lok Sabha MPs announced a merger with the Tripura-based Nationalist Citizens Party of India.
US President Donald Trump signed the 'Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026' into law on Friday, September 18, 2026.
Republican Senator Lindsey Graham, after whom the sanctions bill was named, died in July 2026.
The sanctions bill passed the US Senate in an 86-11 vote in August 2026 and cleared the House of Representatives in a 262-159 vote.
The newly signed US law gives the president authority to impose tariffs of up to 100 percent on imports from the five largest buyers of Russian oil or natural gas, including India and China.
The law extends the Iran Sanctions Act for an additional five years.
India's Ministry of External Affairs warned that the US sanctions legislation could impact India-US bilateral relations and global energy markets.
Under the US bill, countries importing less than 15 percent of Russia's natural gas exports may qualify for an exemption if they take significant steps to reduce imports.

According to the US Energy Information Administration, Russia supplied 3.284 million separative work units of enrichment services to US civilian nuclear operators in 2025, accounting for roughly 26 percent of total purchases.
The US Department of Energy awarded Orano USA a $900 million task order in January 2026 to build domestic uranium enrichment capacity.
India rejected allegations from Pakistan regarding a collision between the Indian warship INS Kolkata and the Pakistani naval vessel PNS Hunain in the Arabian Sea on September 15, 2026.
India summoned Pakistan's Charge d'Affaires Saad Warraich to lodge a strong protest over PNS Hunain's conduct.

Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated that PNS Hunain carried out a dangerous overtaking manoeuvre violating Article 10 of the 1991 bilateral agreement requiring warships to maintain a 3-nautical-mile distance.
INS Kolkata sustained no major damage and remained deployed at sea following the collision, while PNS Hunain was observed returning to harbour after sustaining damage.
Pakistan summoned Indian Charge d'Affaires Satyanjal Pandey and alleged that aggressive manoeuvres by the Indian warship within Pakistan's exclusive economic zone caused the collision.
The last recorded collision between Indian and Pakistani warships occurred in 2011 when INS Godavari was marginally damaged by PNS Babur during anti-piracy operations in the Gulf of Aden.
Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal strongly condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including targets in civilian areas and economic assets.

Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami wrote to External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar in August requesting government intervention for Indramani Nautiyal, an Indian truck driver held in Saudi Arabia over an unpaid fine of approximately 2.29 crore rupees.
